English: Field Plot
A patchwork of staked-out earth, marking the first attempts to till the open plains. Provides basic sustenance and a foundation for further development.
Plow Furrow
Simple wooden plows and hand-dug furrows increase the efficiency of the fields, bringing modest improvement to local harvests and tax yields.
Hay Barn
A simple timber barn for storing hay and fodder, reducing losses and increasing food security. More reliable harvests mean more stable income for the city.
Shepherds Hut
A cluster of simple dwellings for shepherds and their flocks, fostering agricultural settlement and supporting the rural workforce. Livestock and wool trade increase city revenues.
Threshing Floor
A dedicated area for threshing and winnowing, improving grain processing and storage. This organized approach increases both food surplus and trade.
Irrigation Channel
Complex networks of irrigation ditches and channels harness seasonal floods, expanding cultivation and protecting against drought. The bounty of the plains feeds the city.
Plains Mill
A large windmill or watermill serves the community, grinding grain efficiently and supporting a bustling local market. The mill attracts commerce and increases city prosperity.
Crop Rotation Yards
Advanced agricultural practices and managed yards allow for crop rotation, maintaining soil fertility and boosting yields for generations.
Harvest Granary
Vast granaries store the bounty of the plains, stabilizing food supply and allowing the city to withstand poor harvests or siege, while supporting both trade and defense.
Plains Estate
A grand estate presides over the plains, uniting agricultural holdings under efficient stewardship. The estate draws merchants, secures food and wealth, and greatly expands the citys influence.
